findings.namedBuyers: Lyuba Encheva, Communications and Events Coordinator, is the primary operational relationship contact: CITA publishes her name with communication@cita.utoronto.ca, the same role mailbox used on the event pages. The 2024 annual review also credits her with organizing the separate National Jamboree. Shantanu Basu, CITA Interim Director, is a secondary leadership/referral contact; the CITA@40 programme names him for introductory remarks. Neither source establishes guestroom contracting authority. Ling Tan is additionally identified as Department Manager in the 2024 review, but current role and involvement in CITA@40 require confirmation.
findings.futureEdition: None officially announced found as of November 15, 2026. The verified activity dates are May 27–29, 2026, not the 2025 dates embedded in schedule-file URLs. This edition is past and outside the requested horizon. No next-edition dates or city can be populated. The 40th-anniversary branding is not evidence of an annual CITA@40 conference.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown could be considered for a future, separately verified subset of visiting researchers, speakers or VIPs, or a small side meeting; it is not evidenced as a current supplier. A 157-room Harbourfront city hotel is not the on-campus option and cannot claim the campus-location convenience of the listed accommodation pathways. Neither a resort retreat nor moving the scientific programme off campus is supported by this edition. Event attendance, overnight share, peak rooms and room nights are not published as aggregate figures in the reviewed sources, so neither a full buyout nor a 15–109-room opportunity is qualified. Do not assume restaurant/lounge or banquet catering availability; verify internally before offering food-and-beverage functions.
findings.venueCommitments: Historical conference: McLennan Physical Laboratories, University of Toronto, St. George Campus, 60 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Printed programme specifies MP203 and parallel rooms MP102, MP118, MP137 and IdeaLab MP1306. Historical banquet: May 28, 2026, 6:00 PM, Mountbatten Room, Chelsea Hotel, 33 Gerrard Street West. Both venues are in Toronto proper; the conference is on the downtown university campus, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. Chelsea is a competing hotel for banquet business; this does not establish a Chelsea guestroom block. No future venue commitment found.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified examples, not a complete edition timeline: November 14–16, 2003, Kingston Meeting: The Microwave Sky Confronts the Universe, Pacific Institute for Theoretical Physics, University of British Columbia, Vancouver; May 27–29, 2026, CITA@40 Kingston Meeting, University of Toronto, Toronto, with Chelsea Hotel banquet. The 2026 overview says the inaugural Kingston meeting was in Kingston, Ontario, but gives no date. CITA describes Kingston meetings as held at locations around Canada. This supports a travelling scientific-meeting tradition, not an established yearly Toronto hotel rotation. Unrelated CITA-supported conferences and the National Jamboree are not CITA@40 editions.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Historical edition-specific logistics states: "Participants are responsible for booking their own accommodations as we know that better rates can be obtained using the various travel websites and contacting hotels directly." Every listed lodging option: Courtyard Downtown Toronto; Massey College; Chestnut Residence; Oak House; New College; Daphne Cockwell Complex at Toronto Metropolitan University. Chestnut Residence and Oak House each show Group Name CITA@40 and Promo Code CITA; New College shows promotion code CITA2026 for single rooms. These are published booking/promotion pathways, not proof of contracted room quantities. No room-block allocation, housing bureau, exclusive host-hotel agreement or open hotel RFP was found. Chelsea Hotel is separately committed for the historical banquet, not identified as a lodging block. Future hotel sourcing is unconfirmed, not open.
findings.organizationStructure: CITA is a nationally supported academic research centre located at the University of Toronto, not a corporate event agency, PCO or DMC. The conference celebrates the institute and the broader Kingston Meeting community. CITA supports scientific meetings nationally; support or sponsorship is not proof that it centrally purchases accommodation at every meeting. No external housing operator or PCO was identified in the reviewed event material.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The historical lodging page directs delegates to self-book, lists Courtyard Downtown Toronto and five campus/student-residence options, and supplies promotion codes for three residences. This is evidence of alternatives and a decentralized booking route, not hotel exclusivity or sellout. The Chelsea Hotel already held the historical banquet commitment. There is no sourced overflow requirement, rejected room allocation, competitor capacity shortfall, pickup report or displacement evidence. The published warning about FIFA-related rate increases was advice for 2026 bookings, not evidence of future overflow.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Remove the unsupported SALES_READY designation for this edition and retain a historical academic-organizer relationship lead, subject to ORS. Contact Lyuba Encheva at the published event-role mailbox communication@cita.utoronto.ca: ask whether a Toronto-hosted Kingston Meeting or successor programme is planned within December 2026–June 2028; request confirmed dates, venue, overnight-delegate estimate, booking model and accommodation-list decision maker. Ask for an introduction to the responsible administrator only if a live requirement exists; Shantanu Basu is a secondary leadership route, not an assumed hotel buyer. Do not submit an unsolicited full-event/banquet displacement proposal or quote room volumes without a brief.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Not accessible as a forward sales opportunity: May 27–29, 2026 has passed. Historically the conference rooms and Chelsea banquet venue were already specified, while lodging was participant-booked. These facts must not be displayed as currently open inventory or a current RFP.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional relationship-development hypothesis only: if CITA confirms another Toronto meeting with visiting delegates and a self-booking model, seek inclusion of a Radisson booking link or a modest optional allocation alongside the existing accommodation choices. A Kingston Meeting may occur elsewhere in Canada; recurrence of that tradition does not establish a Toronto return, hotel rotation or next CITA@40 edition. No future demand, room quantity or competitive capture is verified.
